target.title: fix(qqbot): soft-wrap exec approval command preview for desktop QQ
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Desktop QQ renders fenced code blocks as a single horizontally scrollable line and does **not** soft-wrap long content, while mobile QQ wraps automatically. As a result, a long command in a QQ Bot exec approval preview was only partially visible on desktop, forcing the approver to drag a horizontal scrollbar to read the full command before approving (issue #101979). This soft-wraps the (already length-capped) command preview at a bounded width before it is placed in the code fence, so the whole command is visible on desktop and still correct on mobile.

The wrapping is now **surrogate-safe**: an earlier version could place a wrap boundary between the high and low surrogate of a non-BMP character (e.g. an emoji), splitting it into two lone surrogates that render as replacement characters. Wrapping now never cuts between a surrogate pair.

Closes #101979.

## Summary

- Soft-wraps the shell command shown in QQ Bot exec approval messages so it wraps inside the code block.
- Approvers on desktop QQ can read the full command at a glance instead of dragging a horizontal scrollbar before approving.
- Wrapping is surrogate-pair-safe so non-BMP characters (emoji) crossing the wrap width are kept intact.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/approval/index.test.ts` — **10 passed** (local), after the surrogate-safety fix:

  ```
  ✓ extension-messaging  extensions/qqbot/src/engine/approval/index.test.ts (10 tests) 62ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  10 passed (10)
  ```

- `wrapCommandPreview` unit tests: short lines unchanged, long lines hard-wrapped ≤ width and losslessly round-trip, existing newlines preserved, non-positive width disables wrapping.
- New regression tests: a non-BMP emoji (`U+1F4A9`, a surrogate pair) positioned so the naive width boundary would fall between its high and low surrogate is **not** split — output round-trips losslessly, contains no lone surrogates, and the emoji survives intact. A width-1 edge case with leading surrogate pairs still makes forward progress.
- `buildExecApprovalText` test proves a 120-char command is wrapped so no code-block line exceeds the wrap width.
- Existing UTF-16-boundary truncation test still proves the surrogate pair is not split by the upstream `truncateUtf16Safe(cmd, 300)` cap.

## Notes

- Wrapping is applied after the existing `truncateUtf16Safe(cmd, 300)` cap, so it never lengthens the underlying command content — it only inserts line breaks for display.
- `wrapCommandPreview` is exported for direct unit testing and future reuse.
- **Behavior proof on a real QQ Desktop client** (screenshot/recording of a long approval wrapping in the actual client) requires a human with a QQ Desktop install; it cannot be produced by an automated agent. The change is validated by the focused unit tests above, which assert the exact wrapping/surrogate behavior that drives what the client renders.
